chunks: Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Hasan ibn Sama'a from Abi Basir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who leads the people in prayer in a narrow place, and there is a screen between them and him, is it permissible for him to lead them in prayer? He said: 'Yes.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the man who leads the people in prayer in a narrow place, and there is a screen between them and him, is it permissible for him to lead them in prayer? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida
key_terms.سِتْرٌ: Screen or curtain used as a partition

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to lead prayer with a screen between the imam and the congregation?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the permissibility of leading prayer in confined spaces with a screen (sitr) is confirmed, reflecting the practical flexibility of Shia jurisprudence regarding congregational settings. This ruling underscores that the validity of the imam's leadership is not contingent upon the followers having a direct, unobstructed line of sight, but rather on the proper formation and intention of the congregation. It highlights the emphasis on communal unity over rigid spatial aesthetics in Islamic worship.
